_podcast.theme_scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Cariboo Voices & Local News' — stories FROM and ABOUT the Cariboo-Chilcotin region and its communities. Score 80-100 for articles directly covering: news and events in Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola, Horsefly, Likely, Anahim Lake, Alexis Creek, or the Cariboo Regional District; local government and civic decisions (City of Williams Lake, City of Quesnel, CRD, District of 100 Mile House); local health services and emergency closures; local economy, businesses, and community programs; Cariboo arts, culture, and community events; AND digital equity, rural internet access (fiber, fixed wireless, Starlink), and connectivity serving these specific communities. Articles from local Cariboo news sources (mycariboonow.com, wltribune.com, quesnelobserver.com, 100milefreepress.net, cfjctoday.com) covering Cariboo community life should score 65-85. Score 50-79 for: BC provincial news directly affecting Cariboo communities, rural Canadian community stories closely paralleling Cariboo life, digital equity and rural internet broadly. Score 20-49 for: general BC news that may affect rural areas, broader rural Canada topics without specific Cariboo tie-in. Score 0-19 for: national/international news without Cariboo relevance, pure tech or entertainment with no community angle. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): international geopolitical and war news with no Cariboo tie-in; science discoveries without a local community connection; consumer tech reviews and gadget guides; wildlife and conservation stories not involving Cariboo communities or First Nations; BC provincial news without direct Cariboo-region relevance. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items._excerpt: A view from downtown Williams Lake late Saturday afternoon Oct. 17. The Social Planning Council continues to work on making a difference in Williams Lake and area through its poverty reduction strategy. At the latest regular city council meeting this month, Angelika Sellick presented an update on the Thrive Poverty Reduction Strategy and the work of the Poverty Reduction Working Group. The working group was formed in 2018 with the strategy that was endorsed by city council published in 2021 following extensive community consultation. “We all know the social planning council is in no way the only organization that is doing poverty reduction work in our community,” Sellick acknowledged, adding they recognize and celebrate the richness of organizations doing poverty reduction in their own communities without any direct connection to the Social Planning Council established in 1995. Through community consultation Sellick said the Social Planning Council has come to understand poverty as the condition in which people lack the resources, means, choices and opportunities to maintain self-sufficiency and a quality of life that supports basic needs, dignity and meaningful participation in the community. The Social Planning Council is a table that meets monthly to learn, share and collaborate on practical action and advocacy leading to increased community social well-being. Some organizations involved are the Salvation Army, Interior Health, Gibraltar Mine, the Foundry Cariboo Chilcotin, Women’s Contact Society, and WorkBC, in addition to representatives from city council. “Poverty is not the outcome of personal deficiencies or lack of will. It is the result of greater systemic failures,” Sellick said further noting poverty reduction work at the local level can contribute and lead to the ending of poverty at a global level. items.title: [ArchDaily] Critical Regionalism Abroad: Aris Konstantinidis without Greece
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Since the 1980s, critical regionalism has been globally celebrated for imbuing modern architecture with local sensibilities. After rising to international stardom, however, several critical regionalists soon began to erect distinctive albeit “placeless” buildings around the world. This book examines how Aris Konstantinidis (1913–1993), a Greek architect less well known outside his home country, instead propagated his vision of regional modernism to global audiences on his own terms through his publishing and teaching beyond national borders.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease. The strongest benefits appeared at 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps, suggesting that the popular 10,000-step goal may not be necessary.
